target.title: refactor(workboard): split store implementation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/workboard/src/store.ts` had grown to more than 4,300 lines and combined persistence, normalization, workflow, enrichment, notifications, and dispatch behavior in one module. That made focused review and maintenance unnecessarily difficult.

Related: #106273

## Why This Change Was Made

Split the implementation into cohesive internal modules while preserving `WorkboardStore` as the public facade. Persistence and mutation serialization remain owned by the core layer; capability layers inherit that single ordering boundary. Public exports, store namespaces, SQLite schema, and runtime behavior remain unchanged.

AI-assisted: yes. The split was mechanically generated, then formatted, typechecked, tested, structurally compared, and independently reviewed in bounded targets.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Maintainers get smaller review surfaces organized by responsibility.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxdjc8c9vv668z5c4gpxgk65`: `corepack pnpm test:extension workboard` — 8 files, 118 tests passed.
- Same Testbox: path-scoped `corepack pnpm check:changed -- <nine Workboard store modules>` — extension/type-test typechecks, lint, formatting, import-cycle, database-first, runtime-sidecar, SDK baseline, and dependency guards passed.
- Same Testbox: `corepack pnpm deadcode:exports` — baseline matched all 3,294 entries after narrowing internal helper visibility.
- Pre/post public method inventory and top-level helper inventory match exactly.
- `git diff --cached --check` passed.
- Autoreview split into four coherent sub-180 KB stack targets because the aggregate mechanical move exceeds the review bundle safety cap; focused unused-export cleanup review also passed.
